prompt: A photographic reference plate: a real photograph, front view, full figure and head-and-shoulders, neutral standing, even light. Not concept art, not an illustration, not a painting, not a render. 9:16 vertical. SUBJECT: an ascetic sage in his sixties, of the line of Kusika. Build: lean and physically hard - the shoulders of a man who once trained. Hair: matted and piled high in a jaṭā, coiled rope-like locks, ash-grey beard. The head is UNCOVERED - no turban, no wrap, no cap, nothing tied over the hair. Complexion: deep warm brown, sun-weathered, and NONE LIGHTER. A plain dusting of pale wood-ash on the skin, shoulders and forearms - the residue of sitting by a fire, uneven and powdery, not applied and not a mark. No painted marks anywhere on him: no red tilak, no forehead stripes, no tripuṇḍra, no coloured paste, no sandal lines. The only thing on his skin is plain pale ash. Dress: cloth draped at the waist, a single upper cloth over one shoulder, bare torso otherwise. The cloth is UNDYED BUT WORN: grey-brown, dust in the weave, thin at the folds, the colour of cloth that has been slept in on the ground. Never clean, never bright, never saffron or orange, and never the clean undyed white that belongs to Vasiṣṭha. Ornament: one thin strand of worn rudrākṣa, half-hidden under the upper cloth, never displayed. No other ornament at all - no layered mālās, no beads at the wrist, no rings. Carries: a plain dark dense-wood staff, shoulder-height, worn pale at the grip, blunt and splayed at the base from years on stone. No carving, no finial. The one thing to get right: his eyes REST on what they look at. They do not search. Must be distinct from VASISHTHA at a glance: matted piled jaṭā against combed and tied hair; ash-grey against white; lean and sun-dark against fuller and softer; cloth grey-brown with dust against cloth clean and undyed white. Cloth is woven, cut from the loom, and draped: antariya at the waist, uttariya over the shoulder. Never tailored, never buttoned. Any ornament a character wears comes from the relief vocabulary - Bharhut, Sanchi, Amaravati: heavy kundala earrings that pull the lobe, flat collars and torques, armlets above the bicep, bangles. Gold that gleams, never glitters. No faceted gems. A character whose dress names no ornament wears none. Faces from the real range of the subcontinent. Nose bridges, eye shapes, jaws and cheeks that vary. Pores, oil sheen, sun on skin that has lived outdoors, age in the neck and hands. Bodies are real. No gym physiques. Barefoot on stone. Never sharpen features to read noble or broaden them to read lowly. photoreal, film grain. uncut draped handloom - no stitched garment.

judging_order: THE FACE FIRST. Before cloth, ash, staff or ornament: is this a face that can carry fourteen shots and still be one person? Age in the neck and hands, eyes that REST rather than search, no beatific smile, no narrowed eyes. A candidate with the right face and wrong cloth is fixable; the reverse is not.
Then the jaṭā: matted rope-like locks piled, head uncovered.
Then the skin: deep warm brown, none lighter, ash as residue and not as a mark.
Then the cloth: grey-brown, dusty, draped, not tailored, not saffron, not clean white.
